title: DynamoDB Advanced Features 🔄
description: Streams, Global Tables, DAX caching, and fine‑grained access control.

slides.title: Capacity Modes: Provisioned vs On‑Demand 💰
slides.content:
# Two Billing Models

- **Provisioned Capacity**: You specify the number of **read capacity units (RCUs)** and **write capacity units (WCUs)** per second. You pay for provisioned capacity even if not used. Use for predictable workloads.
- **On‑Demand Capacity**: Pay per request. No capacity planning. Use for variable, unknown, or spiky traffic. AWS handles scaling instantly.

You can switch between modes once per 24 hours.

slides.title: DynamoDB Streams 🔄
slides.content:
# Capture Changes in Real Time

When enabled, DynamoDB Streams records every item modification (create, update, delete) in order, with the before‑and‑after image.
- Stored for 24 hours.
- You can trigger AWS Lambda functions to react to changes (e.g., send email on new order, replicate to Elasticsearch).
- Integrates with Kinesis Data Streams for extended retention and advanced processing.

This makes DynamoDB a perfect source for event‑driven architectures.

slides.title: Global Tables 🌍
slides.content:
# Multi‑Region, Multi‑Active

DynamoDB Global Tables replicate your table automatically across chosen AWS regions. You can read and write to any replica, and changes are propagated to all regions with low latency.
- Conflict resolution is handled by **last writer wins** (based on timestamp).
- Ideal for globally distributed applications that need local read/write performance.

**Note**: Requires DynamoDB Streams to be enabled, and you cannot disable it after creating a Global Table.

slides.title: DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) ⚡
slides.content:
# In‑Memory Cache

DAX is a fully managed, highly available in‑memory cache that sits in front of DynamoDB. It reduces read latency from milliseconds to **microseconds**.
- Compatible with existing DynamoDB API calls – no code changes except endpoint.
- Best for read‑heavy, latency‑sensitive workloads (gaming leaderboards, real‑time bidding).
- Not a replacement for ElastiCache; it’s tightly coupled to DynamoDB.

Cached data has a default TTL of 5 minutes.

quizData.question: When should you consider using DAX?

options.text: When your DynamoDB reads need microsecond latency and high throughput
When you want a data warehouse
When you need to encrypt data at rest

quizData.explanation: DAX is an in‑memory cache specifically designed to accelerate DynamoDB reads, reducing latency to microseconds.

slides.title: Security & Fine‑Grained Access 🔒
slides.content:
# Beyond IAM

DynamoDB integrates with IAM for table‑level permissions, but also supports:
- **Fine‑grained access control**: restrict access to specific items or attributes based on IAM policy conditions (e.g., a user can only see their own shopping cart).
- **VPC Endpoints**: keep all traffic within the AWS network.
- **Encryption at rest** (enabled by default with AWS‑owned key, can use KMS).
- **Point‑in‑time recovery** (PITR) for continuous backups with per‑second granularity.
